items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I’d probably be at the clubs watching Milt Jackson or Herbie, instead of studying for an exam.

ctx.x: I was going to ask how you ended up there.

Okay, what happened was that I had taken auditions for different schools. I tried Eastman, which I totally messed up. And Manhattan School of Music for some reason I took the theory, to be a theory major. And a student named David Butler had come down to the Music and Art and had talked up Fredonia. So there were about six of us from Music and Art, decided we’d look it up, you know, see what’s up. So I had gotten my teacher because she never was really hot on like Bach. And somehow I felt like I needed to learn…

had already failed Eastman, I wasn’t too happy about New York College of Music and Manhattan School of Music because I felt I’d see myself at the clubs all night with a midterm the next day. Because I’d probably be at the clubs watching Milt Jackson or Herbie, instead of studying for an exam. So I said I need to get out of New York. So I finished the audition and he says, “Well Allan, you know there aren’t many black people in Fredonia.” My thing was I really don’t care, I want to know did I pass the audition or…
